### A Clock with Limits

In a time-isolation experiment, very dim light plus a fixed sleep–wake schedule usually synchronized healthy adults to a 24.0-hour day. But the same system generally failed to adjust to imposed 23.5- or 24.6-hour days. The body can align with a compatible cycle, but it is not a stopwatch that can follow any timetable.

### Timing Can Become a Habit

A Japanese university survey found that 66 of 643 students, or 10.3%, reported a self-awakening habit. Their sleep and wake times were about 30 minutes earlier than those of other students. In a separate small study, participants reached an 82% success rate by day seven after repeated attempts, suggesting that expectation and morning-oriented routines may strengthen this behavior.

## In one line

Waking before an alarm may feel like a private prediction, but it could be a quiet partnership between biological timing and learned expectation.
